text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - UK shares dropped on Friday as a fresh bout of jitters hit Wall Street and gilts dropped sharply amid profit-taking and political jitters after a local election defeat for the ruling Conservative party. The FTSE 100 index closed 30.9 points lower at 4,308.3 a fall of 28.5 since last Friday.

FRANKFURT - German DAX index ends bourse down 0.5 percent from Thursday's records after a bout of profit-taking sparked by overnight losses on Japan and Wall Street and talk of an EMU delay. Dealers see outlook stable at lower levels, but still see potential for more gains next week. The DAX index ended down 17.08 points at 3,259.64 up 75.55 on the week. In post-bourse trade the index fell 11.54 to 3,261.04.

PARIS - French shares closed with a sharp loss, affected by a further 55 point fall in the Dow Jones Industrial Index on Wall Street and profit-taking on the expiry of February futures. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 21.85 points or 0.83 percent at 2,607.55.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed in negative territory but above the day's lows in derivatives-driven trading. "At the moment we are moving on a one-to-one scale to the Dow Jones," one trader noted, adding that the Swiss bourse was following the ups and downs of early Wall Street. The All-share SPI fell 18.57 points to close at 2,851.56 a gain of 19.62 on the week. TOKYO - Tokyo's main stock index closed down 2.44 percent on Friday due to profit taking in some export-orientated blue chips after the yen gained against the dollar in the afternoon session. The Nikkei 225 average was in negative territory for the entire day and ended down 464.56 points at 18,557.00 a drop of 477.54 since last week.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended with heavy losses on Friday as comments made by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan earlier this week returned to haunt the market. The Hang Seng Index tumbled 147.88 points, or 1.09 percent, to close at 13,398.72 a fall of 46.13 from last Friday.

SYDNEY - Australian shares ended lower on Friday with investors still nervous before the weekend following the hawkish comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan made earlier in the week. The All Ordinaries index ended 14.8 points lower at 2,449.9 down 25.4 from a week ago.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial shares end weaker after mixed trading day. Dealers say industrials hit by a weaker Dow Jones index overnight, profit-taking and nervousness over Thursday's "poor" money supply figures. Industrial index dives 79.4 points to 8,244.3 down 135 from a week ago, overall index sheds 50.7 to 7,145.3 a rise of 21.2 since last week and the gold index drops 22.6 points to 1,565.5 up 47.7 from last Friday.
